name_or_item: British Railways Board approved new-wagon programme, average of 1,429 wagons
scope: planned 1970 expenditure GBP 5.2m on 1,429 new wagons; mixed types including high-capacity air-braked stock
source_ref: Hansard, HC Deb 28 April 1970 vol 800 c1024; https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1970/apr/28/railways-rolling-stock
notes: DERIVED average from a stated programme, not an invoice. 458 in 1900 money (general index 795). A measured wagon capital figure for 1970: the nearest earlier measured price is the 1923-24 Gloucester Gas order for a 12-ton private-owner wagon, and the 1963 Liner Train GBP 3,000 is a design case. The average covers a mixed programme, so it sits above a 16-ton mineral wagon and the overhaul percentages taken against it are correspondingly low.

name_or_item: British Railways Board approved new-carriage programme, average of 427 carriages
scope: planned 1970 expenditure GBP 10.7m on 427 new carriages
source_ref: Hansard, HC Deb 28 April 1970 vol 800 c1024; https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1970/apr/28/railways-rolling-stock
notes: DERIVED average from a stated programme. 3152 in 1900 money (general index 795). A measured 1970 carriage capital figure, useful as a check on the 1970 rung of the carriage purchase ladder, which is otherwise interpolated. Not used in this pass beyond that note.

name_or_item: Beeching 1961 wagon functional line per wagon in stock
scope: provision, maintenance, stabling and servicing; capital provision inside
source_ref: The Reshaping of British Railways (1963), p. 6; https://railnews-business.co.uk/docs%20library/1963%20BRB_Beech001a.pdf
notes: MEASURED inputs, DERIVED per wagon: GBP 46.1m over 848,591 wagons. 9.84 in 1900 money (general index 552). Repeated from research-pricing-rows-43.csv to anchor the series; the only measured per-wagon-year figure after 1892 found in any pass.

name_or_item: British Railways short-wheelbase wagon fleet, March 1969
scope: short-wheelbase goods wagons only; the rest of the fleet is not counted
source_ref: Hansard, HL Deb 29 October 1970 vol 312 cc193-4; https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/lords/1970/oct/29/railway-goods-wagons
notes: MEASURED. The question states 330,000 short-wheelbase wagons in March 1969; the answer gives about 260,000 by the end of 1970 and 3,200 new wagons of 15-foot or longer wheelbase since January 1969. Denominator for a fleet-average per-wagon-year cost.

name_or_item: British Railways short-wheelbase wagon fleet at end-1970
scope: short-wheelbase goods wagons only; described in October 1970 as still the vast majority of the fleet
source_ref: Hansard, HL Deb 29 October 1970 vol 312 cc193-4; https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/lords/1970/oct/29/railway-goods-wagons
notes: MEASURED. The projected figure at the end of 1970, not an outturn count. The whole fleet is larger; no verified 1981 count was obtained in this pass.

name_or_item: BR General Repair cycle, HAA and similar wagons, in force before 1992
scope: HAA and similar merry-go-round hoppers; full strip, components repaired or replaced, most wagons re-bodied
notes: STATED (official), resting on BR Engineering Instruction WF/81 of 1980. The only documented BR wagon general-repair interval found. The practice ceased in 1992. Supports a 6-year interval as inside the 5-7 year band, and shows the event was a full strip rather than a running repair.

name_or_item: Serpell, total vehicle maintenance, 1981 out-turn at 1982 prices
scope: day-to-day, light, intermediate and general repairs; all vehicle types; capital out
notes: MEASURED aggregate with no wagon split. 13.6m in 1900 money at the 1982 index 3483, since the report states 1982 prices. Not comparable with a per-wagon-year figure and not used as one.

name_or_item: Serpell, BREL vehicle maintenance and repairs, 1981 out-turn at 1982 prices
scope: heavy maintenance and repairs carried out by British Rail Engineering Limited; all vehicle types; 55 per cent of all maintenance expenditure
notes: MEASURED aggregate with no wagon split. 7.64m in 1900 money at the 1982 index 3483. The report's list of BREL unit-cost rises 1977-81 names locomotives, multiple units, HSTs and coaches but not wagons, which points to wagon repairs being depot work.
